Definition: Paroh, a general title of Egyptian kings
BiblicalUsage: Par'ôh is not a name but the title of every Egyptian king. Pharaoh asks, Who is the LORD, that I should obey His voice, and his heart is hardened; Israel is told to tell their sons that they were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt and the LORD brought them out; and Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title Pharaoh stands for every power that says, Who is the LORD. It hardens, it enslaves, and in the end the LORD brings His people out from under it.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
